implementation_notes: The standard library gives you transactions (database/sql Tx) but nothing that knows about clusters, so the shared lock is written by hand in one of two shapes. Persistence side: inside tx, take the root's lock with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or, when the cluster has no row of its own to lock, pg_advisory_xact_lock(clusterID), then read and write every member; the lock dies with the transaction. In-process side: a map[int64]*sync.Mutex (or sync.Map) keyed by the cluster id, held with defer mu.Unlock() for the whole edit - one lock for root and members. Both replace per-member locking; the database variant is the one that spans processes.
idiom_name: transaction + root-row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / pg_advisory_xact_lock), or a mutex map per aggregate root
pitfalls: database/sql connection pools are meant to be concurrency-safe, but a transaction is bound to one connection: every statement of the edit must use tx, and mixing in db calls escapes the lock.

pg_advisory_xact_lock serializes by the integer/string key you choose, not by the row - a hash collision or a wrong key silently locks a different cluster, so derive the key from the root id explicitly.
A mutex map grows with the number of clusters seen; without eviction (or a sharded/striped map) it becomes a memory leak in long-running services.
